messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you sell your acoustic guitar quickly and safely: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a thorough cleaning (strings, fretboard, body). Tune it to standard pitch. | A well‑presented instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture the front, back, sides, headstock, strings, and any imperfections. Use natural light and a neutral background. | Good photos attract buyers and reduce the chance of disputes over condition. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local music stores. Note price ranges for similar models, ages, and conditions. | Helps you set a realistic price and avoid underselling. | | **4. Write a Detailed Description** | Include brand, model, year, serial number, condition notes, any upgrades, and why you’re selling. | Transparency builds trust and reduces back‑and‑forth questions. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform(s)** | • **Reverb** – great for musical instruments, global reach.
• **eBay** – auction or fixed price, large audience.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local music shops** – consignment or direct sale. | Different platforms reach different buyer types; use a mix if you want speed and price. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | Start slightly above your target to allow room for negotiation. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a higher starting point can still land you a good deal. | | **7. Decide on Shipping vs. Local Pickup** | • **Shipping**: Use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and a reputable carrier (UPS, FedEx, USPS). Get insurance and tracking.
• **Local Pickup**: Meet in a public place, bring a friend, and accept cash or Venmo. | Shipping expands your market but adds cost; local pickup saves money and is safer. | | **8. Prepare Payment Options** | Offer secure methods: cash, Venmo, PayPal (with buyer protection), or bank transfer. Avoid checks unless you verify them. | Reduces fraud risk and ensures you get paid. | | **9. Handle Negotiations Professionally** | Keep communication polite, stick to your minimum price, and be ready to walk away if the offer is too low. | Protects your interests and keeps the process smooth. | | **10. Finalize the Sale** | Once you agree on a price, sign a simple bill of sale (include serial number, condition, date, buyer/seller signatures). | Provides legal proof of transfer and protects both parties. | | **11. Ship or Hand Over** | If shipping, package securely and ship immediately. If local, meet at the agreed spot, hand over keys and paperwork. | Prompt delivery builds buyer confidence and avoids disputes. | ### Quick Tips & Safety Reminders - **Avoid “Too Good to Be True” Offers** – If a buyer offers far above market value, verify their identity and be cautious of scams. - **Meet in Public Places** – For local pickups, choose a busy coffee shop or police station parking lot. - **Keep Records** – Save all emails, messages, and receipts. This helps resolve any post‑sale issues. - **Consider a Trade‑In** – If you’re buying a new guitar, some stores will offer a trade‑in value that can offset the cost. ### Optional Extras - **Appraisal** – If you’re unsure of the instrument’s worth, get a professional appraisal from a reputable dealer or appraiser. - **Consignment** – Let a local shop sell it on your behalf for a commission. You’ll get a higher price but wait longer. - **Bundle Deals** – Offer a bundle (guitar + case + strap) to increase perceived value. --- **Sample Listing (Reverb)** > **Title:** 2015 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition > **Description:** > • Brand: Yamaha > • Model: FG800 > • Year: 2015 > • Serial: 12345678 > • Condition: Minor fret wear, no cracks, fully functional. > • Extras: Original case, strap, and a set of replacement strings. > • Reason for selling: Upgrading to a 12‑string. > **Price:** $350 (negotiable) > **Shipping:** Free shipping within the U.S. (insured). > **Payment:** PayPal or Venmo. > **Contact:** [Your email] Feel free to adapt this template to your chosen platform. Good luck with your sale!

Also mention potential appraisal, trade-in, or consignment. Provide tips for negotiation, safe meeting, payment methods. Also mention legal aspects. Provide a concise guide. No function call needed.
